comparator.sourceNotes: Checked 2026-11-13. Actual current programme API, all 26 selected module payloads, seven-page programme OER, current faculty OER, public route/study pages and cohort-specific archive inspected. The formal route is Modern Middle East Studies; Arabic is the first listed language-package illustration, not a separate formal with-Arabic specialization. OER2.3 and public route require basic regional-language knowledge for MMO; advanced CEFR targets for Arabic/Persian/Turkish/Hebrew specializations are not MMO requirements. The 25 EC Arabic1/2/project sequence and Islam5 form the chosen30EC first-year package alongside30EC common study. Both Arabic2 and project require Arabic1 under OER4.2; module project also mentions instructor permission, not automatic formal waiver. Comparative Literatures10EC requires completed year one; additional all-BA2-language gate is limited to formal language specializations. Seminar5EC and thesis10EC both require completed year one and55ECyear two; current residual Philosophy-of-Science wording requires cohort clarification. Thesis uses supervised research, secondary literature and a bounded primary-source corpus; language-specialization primary-language/summary requirements do not transfer wholesale to MMO, whose summary is English. Distinct components remain60+60+55=175EC. Identical5852VCAAY code/id/uid is repeated; the 30EC elective space is already counted and is not a source of another5EC. Faculty3.1/3.2 requires150ECcompulsory+30ECfree choice: sufficient level, no required-curriculum overlap, approval except recognized30ECLeiden/Delft/Erasmus minors, noHonoursCollege credits. Programme3.2.9 restricts Islam:ReligionandSociety minor depending on specialization and abroad/shadow choice; no doublecount/automatic substitution. Current public pages give academic scope, not the missing replacement. The2025–26 archive explicitly separates entrant cohorts; its unused5ECchoice and approved individual shadow programme cannot be silently adopted for2026entrants. Current regulations listing has no adopted bridge; forward2271 returns current2261 bytes. All175EC and reusable research preserved; no no-match or approval.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: The current 151-course workbook supports genuine bounded regional material in Arabic/Near Eastern narrative, Islamic Mediterranean courts and Persian imperial comparison, alongside historical, political, legal, economic and qualitative methods. The retained 24-course180EC proposal is feasible, with eight advanced courses. These contributions do not resolve external curriculum allocation or by themselves establish final material comparability.

candidateAssessment.concept: Comparative regional history, politics and political economy
candidateAssessment.assessment: A feasible 24-course180EC research proposal develops historical source criticism, comparative political/economic/legal inquiry, qualitative/archival methods and empirical econometrics. Persia, Central Asia and other regional examples supply bounded connections. Much sustained empirical inquiry centres other regions. Final material comparability and the closest response await the external5EC/cohort gate; this is not mechanical infeasibility or a no-match.

candidateAssessment.concept: Middle Eastern cultures, languages and religions
candidateAssessment.assessment: World Myth & Literature explicitly includes Arabic and Near Eastern narratives; Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean includes Islamic courts, exchange and visual/material interpretation. Imperial history and artefact/craft analysis provide real further context. Comparative ethics, media and sociological methods do not establish the entire regional religion/literature/language sequence. Arabic/Persian/Turkish/Hebrew interest directions remain separately assessable after the external gate; grouping this research does not discharge sequential extras or establish an accepted omnibus core. No automatic language-only rejection or no-match.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Middle Eastern Studies bachelor examines the region’s history, societies, religions, languages and politics. This example follows the broad Modern Middle East Studies route, with basic Arabic language study.
